requirements.text: The instrument cluster shall provide an onboard speedometer and an odometer that comply with all requirements of UN R39.
The instrument cluster shall comply with all UN R39 requirements for every speedometer and odometer display fitted to the vehicle.
The instrument cluster shall not display graduations or numerical values additional to those permitted by UN R39 on the speedometer.
The instrument cluster shall place the speedometer display within the driver's direct field of view and make it clearly legible both day and night.
The instrument cluster shall provide a speed display range wide enough to include the maximum speed of the vehicle type stated by the manufacturer.
For the M1 vehicle, the instrument cluster speedometer shall use a graduation of 1, 2, 5 or 10 km/h.
The instrument cluster shall indicate speed values at intervals not exceeding 20 km/h when the highest value on the display does not exceed 200 km/h.
The instrument cluster shall indicate speed values at intervals not exceeding 30 km/h when the maximum value on the display exceeds 200 km/h.
Where the instrument cluster offers a km/h / mph setting, it shall display the speed in only one of the two units at any one time.
The instrument cluster shall permanently display the speed unit corresponding to the selected display mode.
For M1 vehicles sold in countries where imperial units are used, the instrument cluster speedometer shall also be marked in miles per hour with graduations of 1, 2, 5 or 10 mph.
The instrument cluster shall indicate mph speed values at intervals not exceeding 20 mph, commencing at 10 or 20 mph.
The instrument cluster shall never indicate a speed lower than the true speed of the vehicle.
The instrument cluster shall maintain, at each UN R39 test speed, the relation 0 ≤ (V1 - V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 4 km/h between displayed speed V1 and true speed V2.
The instrument cluster shall make the odometer display visible or accessible to the driver.
The instrument cluster odometer shall display at least an integer number composed of a minimum of 6 numerals for the M1 vehicle.
For M1 vehicles sold in countries where imperial units are used, the instrument cluster odometer shall be marked in miles.
The instrument cluster shall display the odometer distance in the unit corresponding to the predominant speedometer scale.
Where the driver can select the odometer unit independently of the speedometer, the instrument cluster shall identify the odometer unit in use.
The instrument cluster total distance indicated shall not deviate by more than ±4.0 per cent from the true distance travelled determined per Annex 4.

Where the instrument cluster provides total distance values over the serial data port on the standardised data link connector, those values shall not deviate from the rounded total distance indicated.
The instrument cluster shall provide the total distance values and the total distance indicated with a resolution of 1 km or better (1 mile or better where miles are used).
The instrument cluster shall provide a malfunction indication to the driver in the case of an electrically detectable failure preventing the odometer requirements from being met.
The instrument cluster malfunction indication shall become active when the malfunction occurs and remain active as long as the malfunction persists.
The instrument cluster shall repeat the odometer malfunction indication each time the ignition or vehicle master control switch is activated.
The instrument cluster shall protect the total distance indicated and the total distance values against manipulation (tampering).
The instrument cluster shall, for conformity of production speedometer testing of the M1 vehicle, satisfy 0 ≤ (V1 - V2) ≤ 0.1 V2 + 6 km/h.
The instrument cluster odometer shall increment at integers throughout a minimum 10 km (or 7 mile) test drive so the true distance can be read at each integer transition.
The instrument cluster, as an ESA, shall carry the UN R10 approval mark when approved as an ESA under this Regulation.
The instrument cluster shall display the international approval mark in the conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
The instrument cluster's UN R10 approval marking need not be visible once the cluster is installed in the vehicle.
The instrument cluster shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle complies with UN R10 requirements in normal conditions of use.
The instrument cluster shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The instrument cluster broadband radiated emissions shall stay below the ESA limits of 62 to 52 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz and the corresponding limits up to 1,000 MHz.
The instrument cluster shall keep measured broadband emission values below the ESA type approval limits.
The instrument cluster narrowband radiated emissions shall stay below the ESA limits of 52 to 42 dBµV/m from 30 to 75 MHz and the corresponding limits up to 1,000 MHz.

The instrument cluster shall withstand, over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band, radiated immunity test levels of 60 V/m (stripline), 75 V/m (TEM cell), 60 mA (BCI), 30 V/m (ALSE) and 21 V/m (reverberation chamber), plus 10 V/m (ALSE) and 7 V/m (reverberation chamber) above 2 GHz.

The instrument cluster shall withstand, as minimum levels over the whole 20 MHz to 6 GHz band, 50 V/m (stripline), 62.5 V/m (TEM cell), 50 mA (BCI), 25 V/m (ALSE) and 18 V/m (reverberation chamber), plus 8 V/m (ALSE) and 6 V/m (reverberation chamber) above 2 GHz.
The instrument cluster shall show no degradation of its immunity related functions (speed display, odometer and warning tell-tales) during radiated immunity testing.
For a 12 V system, the instrument cluster shall meet functional performance status III for test pulses 1 and 2a (500 pulses, -75 V and +37 V) where related to immunity related functions.

For a 12 V system, the instrument cluster shall meet functional performance status II for pulse 2b (+10 V, 10 pulses) and status I for pulse 3a (-112 V, 1 h) with respect to its immunity related functions.
The instrument cluster shall, under the 50 km/h immunity test mode, operate in normal mode and show neither unexpected warnings nor inconsistent variation of the odometer.
